findings.claim: The QA route drives the one-paragraph hands-on instructions beginning at html-css-js/html-and-css/accessibility-basics/artifact.html:241, but neither the route nor the artifact presents each task as numbered where-to-look, what-to-type-or-press, what-to-expect, and how-to-know-done steps. The current route can therefore pass while the captain-required instruction shape is absent.
findings.recommendation: Rewrite each hands-on task as an accessible numbered list with explicit where, action, expected result, and done criterion, without exposing the reasoning answer; update the QA path to assert that structure while retaining the same behavioral route.

findings.claim: The manifest records modeledWorstPath as modeledP50 + 2.50 minutes, while the review direction fixes this module route at modeledP50 + 2.0. The result is conservative and remains under 15 minutes, but it does not use the required model.
findings.recommendation: Recalculate modeledWorstPath as modeledP50 + 2.0, update the basis text, and derive budget/aboutLabel from that corrected value without exceeding the 15-minute ceiling.

findings.claim: The page says an informative image needs alt text "saying what it shows." WCAG requires a text alternative that serves the equivalent purpose and conveys the same information in context; literal visual description is not the general rule and is wrong for functional images, images of text, and many complex images.

evidence.section: Intent of Non-text Content: text alternatives convey the same information and serve the same purpose as non-text content

findings.recommendation: Teach that informative alt conveys the image’s relevant information or purpose in context. Keep alt="" for purely decorative images, and avoid implying that every informative image should be visually described.
